infoText.about: Showing up is the goal. After 50, consistency is more important than sets or reps. Keep moving, stay injury-free, feel good doing it.
infoText.setsAndReps: I usually do 3 sets with a 1/2 weight add-on finisher. Somewhere between 10 and 15 reps where the last few feel like work but form never breaks. Rest usually 2 minutes per set.
infoText.floor: Three movements per session. Primary option first, alternative after the slash — use whichever is free. No supersets, no circuits. Do your sets, rest, move on.
infoText.burnout: Optional. Drop your main compound to 50–60% of working weight and take it to failure. Aim for 20–30 reps. Maintains muscle without heavy loading.
infoText.mat: Over time you should develop your own stretch and core routine using the suggestions here. What we suggest here augments what you already know. The hamstring stretch is a daily constant. Everything else rotates. Props are always optional.
infoText.whenToGo: No streaks. No guilt. The app picks up exactly where you left off — tomorrow or next week, it does not matter.

rules.moveOn: Hit the target with clean form 2 sessions in a row.
rules.regress: Pain, a giving-out feeling, form breaking down, or can't reach the bottom of the range.

phases.name: Phase 1: Foundation
phases.goal: Straight-arm shoulder stability, overhead strength, core line and wrist tolerance before going inverted.
warmup: Wrist rocks on all fours: 10 fingers forward, 10 back
Wrist push-ups (rock up onto fingers): 2 x 10

days.name: Day A: Push · Mat → Machines
days.after: Machines (optional): legs only. No extra pressing.

days.name: Day C: Skill & Core · Mat
days.after: Finish: seated pike stretch 2 x 30s. Machines (optional): legs.

ladders.name: Mat · Plank progression
ladders.cue: Hold first, then the single-arm work in the same set. On the wall: back your feet up and place your toes at the mark, press toes into the wall, hands stay planted. Shift weight slowly, grip the floor, stop before the shoulder gives. Wall marks at 1, 2 and 3 ft (tape or wall features). Roller step: press it with a foot first to check it's wedged before putting weight on it. Have a medicine ball? Rolling it under one hand works for the fingertip-hover step too.

steps.name: Floor plank: 30s hold, then 10 weight shifts
Floor plank: 30s hold, then 6 fingertip hovers each side (palm up onto fingertips, then lift 1 inch)
Floor plank: 20s hold, then 6 shoulder taps each side
Feet on the low bar (~4"): 20s hold, then 6 shoulder taps each side
Feet on foam roller on the low bar, wedged against the wall (~10"): 20s hold, then 6 shoulder taps each side
Feet on wall at 1 ft: 20s hold only
Feet on wall at 1 ft: 20s hold, then 6 shoulder taps each side
Feet on wall at 2 ft: 20s hold, then 4 shoulder taps each side
Feet on wall at 3 ft: 20s hold, then 3 shoulder taps each side

ladders.name: Mat · Pike hold
ladders.cue: Ears between biceps, chest toward thighs.

ladders.name: Mat · Pike shrugs
ladders.cue: Elbows locked, full range, pause at the top.

ladders.name: Mat · Pike push-ups
ladders.cue: Head lands slightly in front of hands, elbows back at 45°.

ladders.name: Machines · Dip support hold
ladders.cue: Shoulders pushed down, away from ears. No jumping: use the station's built-in steps to get into position.

steps.name: Support hold, feet lightly on floor

ladders.name: Machines · Assisted dips
ladders.cue: Kneel or stand on the pad. Shoulders pushed down away from your ears, only go as deep as feels stable. Less weight on the stack = harder.

steps.name: Assisted dip machine, moderate assist, 3s lowering

ladders.name: Machines · Overhead press
ladders.cue: Barbell. Ribs down. Drop to 2 x 5 after pike push-ups.

ladders.name: Machines · Single-arm overhead hold
ladders.cue: One weight, one arm at a time. Arm locked, biceps by ear, no leaning. Add 5 lb only when there's zero wobble.

ladders.name: Mat · Dead bugs
ladders.cue: Lower back flat.

ladders.name: Mat · Hollow hold
ladders.cue: Exhale, ribs down. Shorten the hold before letting the back arch.

ladders.name: Mat · Band external rotations
ladders.cue: Light band, slow, elbow tucked at your side. Pain-free.

ladders.name: Machines · Inverted rows
ladders.cue: Body straight, pull chest to the bar, squeeze shoulder blades together.

ladders.name: Machines · Pulldown → assisted pull-ups
ladders.cue: No jumping. Step up onto the machine's platform to reach the bar. Shoulders pulled down first, then pull with the arms. Lower slowly.

ladders.name: Machines · Y-T-W raises
ladders.cue: Slow, thumbs up, squeeze the shoulder blades. Shoulder stability without hanging.

steps.name: Face down on incline bench, no weight

ladders.name: Mat · Side plank (forearm)
ladders.cue: Elbow under shoulder, hips high, body in one line.

ladders.name: Machines · Supported hang
ladders.cue: Bar about head height, feet stay on the floor, lean back into a long banana stretch. Take as much weight on your feet as you need. Shoulders stay active, not dangling.

steps.name: Supported hang, most weight on feet
Supported hang, less weight on feet
Supported scap pulls, feet on floor

ladders.name: Mat · Forearm headstand prep
ladders.cue: Elbows shoulder-width, press forearms into the floor and push the chest toward your legs.

steps.name: Dolphin hold, feet walked in a little
Dolphin hold, feet walked in, shoulders over elbows

ladders.name: Mat · Ball rollout
ladders.cue: Ribs down, glutes squeezed, back flat. Only roll as far as you can without your lower back sagging. Ab wheel instead? It's much harder: only after full ball rollouts, kneeling, rolling toward a wall to limit range.

steps.name: Kneeling, forearms on ball, short roll out
Kneeling, roll out until arms are overhead

ladders.name: Mat · Slow leg lowers
ladders.cue: Lower back pressed into the floor. Only lower as far as you can without it lifting. This trains the controlled lowering for donkey kicks.

phases.graduation: Reach the last step of every ladder and hit its target.
extraChecks: Wrist rocks: 20 reps, pain-free the next day
One full week with no shoulder pain or slipping feeling

ladders.cue: Every rep: 3-second lowering. Arms locked, shoulders stay over your hands. If you can't control the lowering, go back a step.

Ball pike, hips halfway up, 3s return
Ball pike, hips over hands, 3s return
Rock and hold: feet light 2s, lower toes slowly

Donkey kick, hips over hands, 3s lower

ladders.cue: Push tall, ears between biceps. Walk your hands in toward the wall until your hips are high. Wall heights: tape marks (or wall features) at 1 ft, 1.5 ft, 2 ft, 3 ft and 4 ft.

Pike hold, feet on wall at 1 ft
Pike hold, feet on wall at 2 ft, hips high

ladders.name: Mat · Pike compression

ladders.name: Mat · Hollow body
ladders.cue: Lower back flat the whole time.

ladders.name: Machines · Dips
ladders.cue: Only as deep as feels stable. No jumping: use the station's built-in steps to get into position.

steps.name: Assisted dip machine, light assist, 3s lowering

ladders.name: Machines · Overhead press

ladders.name: Machines · Single-arm overhead hold

One-leg L-sit, switch legs each set

ladders.cue: No jumping. Step up onto the machine's platform to reach the bar. Shoulders pulled down first, then pull with the arms. Lower slowly. Slow 3s lowering on each rep.

ladders.name: Machines · Y-T-W raises

ladders.name: Mat · Forearm headstand prep
ladders.cue: Forearms carry the weight, never your head and neck. Any neck pain: stop. Back of the head near the wall for the tuck.
